question: What did this stock return beyond its factor exposures, and does it hold up without hindsight?

in_sample.caption: Residual return = excess return minus factor exposures, alpha included. In-sample: betas fitted on 2024-08-08 to 2026-09-30, so the residual return equals the regression alpha exactly.

point_in_time.caption: Residual return with each day's betas estimated from the previous 252 trading days only. Covers 2025-07-29 to 2026-09-30; the first 252 days are warm-up.

gap.caption: Same days (2025-07-29 to 2026-09-30) for both series. Out-of-sample here refers to the betas; both series share the same days and stock-specific news.
gap.message: In-sample alpha holds up out-of-sample with point-in-time betas (100% kept) and is distinguishable from zero. This rules out hindsight in the betas, not luck and not a missing factor.

chart.caption: Cumulative residual return, compounded daily. Both lines start at zero on 2025-07-28 and cover the same days. In-sample uses betas fitted on the whole period; point-in-time uses betas from the previous 252 days.

rolling_alpha.caption: Each point uses the previous 252 trading days, ending on that date; alpha and betas are both refitted in each window.

non_overlapping.caption: Separate one-year windows counted back from 2026-09-30. Corrected for testing 2 windows (Benjamini-Hochberg).

split_half.caption: One split, fixed in advance at the middle of the period. Betas are refitted in each half.

calendar_years.caption: Sum of daily residual returns within the year (not compounded). In-sample column: betas from the whole period. Point-in-time column: betas from the previous 252 days.

diagnostics.caption: Informational checks at the 5% level, not corrected for multiple testing.
findings: No clear day-to-day correlation in residual returns.
Residual returns have more extreme days than a normal distribution. Intervals are approximate.
No clear clustering of residual volatility.

caveats: You see the stock's return after removing what its five factor exposures explain. It includes alpha.
In-sample: betas are fitted on this same period, so the in-sample line always drifts by the regression alpha. A line ending above zero is not evidence of skill; check the t-statistic.
Point-in-time: each day uses betas from the previous 252 trading days only. It removes hindsight in the betas, but it uses the same days, so it cannot rule out luck.
The lines compound a paper long-short hedge, rebalanced daily, before trading costs, financing and borrowing fees.
Past residual return does not predict future residual return.

warnings.message: Synthetic data for tests and layout checks; not a real ticker.
